scope: LibreCAD_3 root reattachment when the writer regenerates selected IMAGEDEF and IMAGEDEF_REACTOR records.
reproduction: A locally generated custom dictionary referenced a raw IMAGEDEF_REACTOR. Root planning counted it as emitted even though writeObjects skipped it, so the custom root was reattached and the loss count was too low.
implementation: Use one shared IMAGE detection and regeneration predicate for both raw emission and root graph planning. When an image is present, skipped IMAGEDEF/IMAGEDEF_REACTOR records no longer satisfy source raw graph closure.
validation: The generated reactor-reference control fails before the fix: LC_REACTOR is reattached and only one loss is reported.
After the fix LC_REACTOR is not reattached and both incomplete roots are reported; six focused persistence tests pass, including cyclic/shared and no-image root controls.

A named-block-only image reproduced the same false closure before the follow-up. Model-space, named-block and anonymous *U1 block controls now report both incomplete roots; the shared detector excludes regenerated dimension blocks.

A generated reactor with application-group metadata reproduced a separate missing loss report before dc705b90. Model-space, named-block and anonymous-block controls now report the skipped IMAGEDEF_REACTOR as well as the two incomplete roots; six focused persistence tests pass.
All 80 DxfRoundTripTest cases passed on consumer commit dc705b90 with the current locally linked codec.
limits: This is a guard and loss-reporting correction, not IMAGE graph preservation. Detached raw dictionaries may still need output cleanup or full source graph replay, with independent proof. Paper-space, regenerated dimension blocks and other special layouts are not qualified by these controls.
Generated DXF input remains temporary and is not committed.

Source IMAGEDEF and IMAGEDEF_REACTOR records skipped in favor of regenerated records are conservatively reported as lost: metadata and identity equivalence have not been established. The output can be partially written.
